x_en.article_excerpt: Building voice profiles for AI editor: hand-curated few-shots beat random sampling because of cache stability.

parts: Random few-shot sampling kills your prompt cache.
I learned this the boring way — debugging $40 of Anthropic spend that should have been $4.
If your few-shot examples rotate, every call is a cache miss.
Hand-curate 3-5 stable examples. Pin them. Cache them.
The 'random for diversity' instinct is wrong here — diversity comes from the user's article, not the prompt prefix.
Net effect on my voice editor pipeline: $1/mo instead of $10, and zero quality regression.

li_en.article_excerpt: Three weeks of cron-based queue, then switched to Postgres SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

ideal_draft.body:
This post was drafted with Claude and edited by hand.

For three months I ran a custom in-memory job queue for a side project. It mostly worked — until it didn't.

The rebuild took half a Saturday. Postgres outbox + SKIP LOCKED replaced 200 lines of cron + node-schedule with five tables and two SELECTs.

What I learned:

- 'Lightweight' usually means 'I haven't hit the failure mode yet'.
- Postgres locks are not scary; they are a feature. SKIP LOCKED was added in 9.5 and most engineers I know still haven't tried it.
- Reaching for Redis is a reflex; reaching for the database you already have is a habit worth building.

Full write-up with the exact schema and a benchmark: artka.dev/blog/multi-agent-postgres
